To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the policymaker prefers a tariff over a quota if the policymaker's utility function is strictly convex, (2) if the policymaker is risk neutral, then the policymaker will prefer a quota if the elasticity of demand exceeds the elasticity of supply, and (3) a tariff is preferred if the policymaker can commit to the quota level, but not if the policymaker cannot commit.

a quota is superior to a tariff when the policymaker can extract rents, when the policymaker is revenue-seeking, and when the domestic firm is a monopoly.

the political economy of trade policy in developing countries, and the choice of tariffs versus quotas as instruments of commercial policy.
the choice of protective instruments under autocracy.
the choice between tariffs and quantitative restrictions, with particular reference to developing economies.

the use of tariffs as an instrument of protection in developing economies may be less a matter of economic efficiency than it is of political economy.
